name: Rate Decision Forecasting Council
description: Seven expert panelists forecast whether the central bank cuts rates at its next meeting: sealed initial ballot, open deliberation until everyone is ready, sealed final ballot.

brief.situation: You sit on a forecasting council of seven experts. The question: will the central bank cut its policy rate at its next meeting, three weeks from now? Public briefing: policy rate 4.50%, unchanged for the last two meetings. Headline CPI 2.9% y/y (down from 3.4% six months ago); core CPI 3.1% and sticky in services. Unemployment 4.3%, up from 3.9% over six months; payroll growth has slowed to roughly a third of last year's pace. GDP grew 0.3% q/q last quarter. The last statement dropped the phrase 'further tightening may be warranted' and said risks are 'more balanced' and decisions are 'data-dependent'. Rate futures imply about a 55% chance of a cut. One CPI print and one jobs report land before the meeting.
brief.rules: The session has three stages. 1) Initial ballot: privately submit your probability (0-100%) that the bank cuts, with a one-line rationale. 2) Discussion: the initial ballots are revealed and the council talks in a shared chat over several passes. On your turn you may post a message, revise your working estimate, and mark yourself ready. Any new message un-readies everyone, so the discussion ends when a full pass goes by with everyone ready and no new messages, or when the pass cap is reached. 3) Final ballot: privately submit your final probability. Some panelists hold private information that only they can see; you decide whether and how to share yours. You are scored on the accuracy of your final ballot, not on agreeing with anyone.

roles.panelist: You are an expert panelist. Bring your own expertise and prior, read the others' arguments carefully, update when the evidence warrants it, and hold your ground when it does not.

panelist.description: An expert on the forecasting council.

lens.description: How this panelist tends to read the evidence.

working.description: Current working estimate shown during discussion (%).

props.expertise: former central bank staff economist; policy reaction functions
props.lens: Committees move slowly and telegraph cuts; a cut without explicit guidance is rare.

props.expertise: rates strategist; futures and swaps pricing
props.lens: Market pricing aggregates information well; deviations need a strong reason.
props.private_info: Your desk's client flow shows large real-money accounts adding receive-fixed positions this week, and two primary dealers you trust privately put the cut at 70%.

props.lens: The labor market leads the policy turn; a cooling job market forces the bank's hand.
props.private_info: Your research team's unpublished regional hiring survey (large sample, historically tracks official payrolls closely) points to the coming jobs report being flat to slightly negative.

props.expertise: inflation economist; former fiscal council member
props.lens: Sticky services inflation keeps central banks cautious; they fear cutting too early more than too late.

props.expertise: central bank communications and committee politics
props.lens: Read the committee, not the data: who votes, what they said, and what they need to see.
props.private_info: At an off-record roundtable last week, two voting committee members separately stressed there was 'no urgency' and that they want 'at least two more months of services inflation data'.

props.lens: External conditions matter: a weak currency or energy shock ties the bank's hands.
props.private_info: Your contacts in energy markets expect a supply cut announcement next week that could add roughly 0.3 percentage points to headline inflation within two months.

props.expertise: generalist superforecaster; base rates and calibration
props.lens: Start from the base rate, adjust modestly, avoid overconfidence in stories.
props.private_info: Your base-rate study: after a statement shifts to 'balanced risks / data-dependent' language, this bank cut at the very next meeting 35% of the time and within two meetings 70% of the time.

cast_initial.description: Submit your sealed initial probability that the bank cuts at the next meeting, with a one-line rationale. Others see it when discussion opens.

probability.description: Chance of a cut, in percent (0-100).

rationale.description: One line: the main reason for your number.

when.why: You have already cast your initial ballot.

say.description: Post a message to the council chat (an argument, evidence, a question to someone). Posting un-readies everyone so they can respond.

revise_estimate.description: Update your publicly visible working estimate during discussion. It is not your final ballot.

probability.description: Your current estimate of a cut, in percent.

when.why: You have no initial ballot to revise.

then.fail: That is already your working estimate; post a message or mark yourself ready instead.

revise_estimate.announce: {$actor.name} revised their working estimate from {$old|1}% to {$params.probability|1}%.

mark_ready.description: Say you have nothing more to add for now. Ends your turn. A new message from anyone will un-ready you.

cast_final.description: Submit your sealed final probability that the bank cuts at the next meeting. This is the ballot you are scored on.

probability.description: Chance of a cut, in percent (0-100).

when.why: You have already cast your final ballot.

stages.name: initial_ballot
stages.brief: Initial ballot. Read the briefing and your private information, then cast your sealed probability with cast_initial.

do: $it.initial_why = 'no ballot submitted; recorded at stated prior'

stages.name: discussion
stages.brief: Discussion. Read the new messages, respond if you have something that moves the question, revise your working estimate if your view changed, and mark_ready when you have nothing more to add.

on_enter.say: Initial ballots are revealed and the discussion is open.

stages.name: final_ballot
stages.brief: Final ballot. Weigh everything you heard and cast your sealed final probability with cast_final.

you.title: You
you.show: {name} — {expertise}. Your lens: {lens} Your starting inclination: about {prior|0}%.

private_info.title: Private information (only you can see this)

council_state.title: Council
council_state.show: Working estimates: mean {$avg(panelist, $it.working)|1}%, range {$min(panelist, $it.working)|1}–{$max(panelist, $it.working)|1}%. Ready: {$count(panelist, $it.ready)}/{$count(panelist)}. Messages so far: {$len($records(chat))}.

aggregate_shift.description: Change in mean probability, final minus initial (points).

final_stdev.description: Population standard deviation of final ballots (points).

initial_stdev.description: Population standard deviation of initial ballots (points).

biggest_mind_change.description: Panelist whose ballot moved the most.

abstentions.description: Ballots filled in by default because a panelist did not vote.

consensus_reached.description: Everyone marked ready before the pass cap.

with.rationale: My prior from my own field.

with.text: I stay near my prior; I have not seen evidence that moves me.
'The council average is ' + $text($round($avg(panelist, $it.working), 1)) + '%; I will move toward it.'
